title: Model intake go-to-market brief and cross-team stitch plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational go-to-market brief and per-team stitch plan for onboarding a new open model to the Redwood catalog. Objective is to coordinate catalog entry, benchmark publication, docs and sample prompts, release notes, and announcement assets so the model is discoverable, performant, and launch-ready across hosted/dedicated/private offerings.
checklist: Catalog: Add model metadata card (name, tags, size, license, recommended variants) and confirm model artifact digest and compatibility flags
Benchmarks: Run microbenchmarks (latency P50/P95 per seq len), throughput sweep, and quality evals on standard prompt suites; publish results as a single MLPerf-like table
Runtime sign-off: Validate kernel selection and quantization profile on required GPU tiers; document expected cost/per-token estimates
Docs: Draft quickstart, API examples (generation, chat, embeddings if applicable), and structured output examples with sample prompts
Release notes: Draft end-user release notes and changelog entry; include known limitations and recommended usage patterns
Security & compliance: Confirm license & export controls; if customer-sensitive, flag for security review
Console: Create per-model dashboard and pre-configured traces for latency SLOs; add default alerting thresholds
Samples & Demos: Prepare 2 reference apps (one chat flow, one retrieval-augmented example) and sandbox notebook
Comms: Coordinate blog draft, product announcement copy, social assets, and support FAQ
Rollout: Define staged rollout plan (canary % traffic, gate metrics, fallback variant) across hosted/dedicated/private
Support readiness: Update runbook for known failure modes and escalate path; schedule a 30-minute handoff with CS/Support
Telemetry: Add model-specific metric tags for cost, token counts, rerate errors, and hallucination-rate proxies
acceptance_criteria: Model appears in catalog with complete metadata and a public 'recommended' variant
Benchmarks published and linked in catalog card; P95 latency meets target for at least one recommended config
Docs quickstart and examples published in docs site and referenced from catalog card
Release notes finalized and scheduled for the release date; comms assets approved by design and legal
Rollout plan documented with clear rollback criteria and automated fallback configured
No outstanding security or license flags blocking public listing
release_notes_draft: New: Added support for 'Atlas-7B' (open-license) — recommended for low-latency chat and embedding-friendly flows. Benchmarks: P50 latency 48ms @ 256 tokens (g4dn-like), Quality: top-line eval pass-rate 87% on intent-suite. Limitations: performance degrades with long-context workloads >2048 tokens; consider medium variant for retrieval-augmented setups. Known issues: occasional tokenization mismatch on legacy tokenizers; see docs for migration steps.
comms_plan: Draft blog post w/ benchmark highlights and reference apps (owner: Aisha)
Design: hero image + 3 social sizes (owner: Rina)
Sales one-pager + pricing guidance for Dedicated usage (owner: Marcus)
Internal announcement + launch sync across Eng, Research, CS, Sales (schedule 2026-03-24)
Public announcement: coordinate timing with region rollout windows
rollout_plan: Day 0: Catalog listing gated (internal-only) with monitoring enabled
Canary 1: 5% hosted traffic for 24h, monitor P95 latency and error rate
Canary 2: 25% hosted traffic and read-only Dedicated availability test
Full: 100% listing and enable default route with cost-warning banner
Private: notify customers with Private deployments and offer migration guide
Fallback: automatic route to 'Atlas-quant' variant if P95 latency exceeds threshold for >30min
kpis: P50/P95 latency targets per recommended config
Adoption: number of distinct API keys using model in first 30 days
Cost per 1K tokens for recommended configs
Mean time to rollback for failed canary (target < 15m)
Support tickets related to model (target: < 10 in first week)
